_readme: KANSAS HOLIDAY CALENDAR -- 2026, twelve dates, from the Judicial Branch's own
published schedule. This is the fourth limb of K.S.A. 60-206(a)(6), 'any day
observed as a holiday by order of the Kansas supreme court'.
Note TWO days for Thanksgiving, and Independence Day published as Friday 3
July. Adding 2027 means fetching that year's schedule, not extending a rule.

authority.citation: K.S.A. 60-206(a)(6), "any day observed as a holiday by order of the Kansas supreme court", as published in the Kansas Judicial Branch holiday schedule
authority.quote: State courts are closed on holidays observed by the Kansas judicial branch. ... 2026 New Year's Day January 1 (Thursday) ... Independence Day July 3 (Friday) ... Thanksgiving November 26 (Thursday) November 27 (Friday) Christmas Day December 25 (Friday)
authority.note: THE FOURTH LIMB OF THE STATUTORY DEFINITION, AND THE ONE THAT GOVERNS COURTS. K.S.A. 60-206(a)(6): "'Legal holiday' means any day declared a holiday by the president of the United States, the congress of the United States or the legislature of this state, OR ANY DAY OBSERVED AS A HOLIDAY BY ORDER OF THE KANSAS SUPREME COURT." This calendar is that last limb -- the Judicial Branch's own published annual schedule at kscourts.gov/Footer/Holiday-Schedule, which lists 2025 and 2026 side by side. TWO DAYS FOR THANKSGIVING -- 26 and 27 November 2026, both listed. Only Wisconsin, South Carolina and Maryland also carry a day after Thanksgiving, and Kansas prints it as part of the same holiday rather than under its own name. INDEPENDENCE DAY IS PUBLISHED AS FRIDAY 3 JULY because 4 July 2026 is a Saturday. The schedule states the observed date directly, so nothing is derived from a shift rule -- the same transcription approach used for Arkansas and Maryland. WHY THIS IS NOT THE WISCONSIN PROBLEM, and the distinction matters: the schedule says a court "may defer observing a holiday if it will interfere with judicial proceedings in progress" and that a district court "may remain open on any of these designated holidays" with approval. Wisconsin's statute keys its rollover on whether the clerk's office IS CLOSED, so a county staying open destroys the list as a proxy. KANSAS KEYS ON THE DAY BEING OBSERVED BY ORDER OF THE SUPREME COURT -- a statewide legal fact -- so a district court opening its doors does not stop the day being a legal holiday for 60-206 purposes. The list IS the test here; in Wisconsin it was not. NOT HERE, AND EARLY: a day declared ad hoc by the President or Congress after this schedule was published is a legal holiday under the first two limbs and cannot be anticipated. A HALF HOLIDAY is expressly NOT a holiday -- "A half holiday is considered as other days and not as a holiday" -- and is correctly absent. 2026 ONLY: the schedule publishes 2025 and 2026 and no later year. A year it does not cover is REFUSED rather than derived.
